title: Seven Riffles
pitch: A night-shift dealer swears three riffles is plenty. The visitor cuts a 52-card deck and releases a riffle, watches the rising sequences fan out like strands, and sees a meter of how far the whole riffle process still sits from a truly random deck, computed exactly on the page. Then an audit runs thousands of seeded shuffles at 1 to 10 riffles and charts which simple tests (top card, suit runs, card guessing) stop betraying the opening order, and when.
whyNow: Timeless: the seven-shuffles slogan is half-known, and which yardstick you pick changes the verdict, which makes it a good argument to lose.

research.summary: The Gilbert-Shannon-Reeds model cuts a deck at a binomially distributed point and interleaves the two piles with probability proportional to pile sizes. Bayer and Diaconis showed that the chance of any deck order after m riffles depends only on its number of rising sequences r, as C(2^m + n - r, n) / 2^(mn), so the distance from uniform for 52 cards can be computed exactly by grouping orders by r (Eulerian counts) and compared with Monte Carlo. Total variation distance stays near 1 at five riffles, is about 0.924 at five, 0.614 at six and 0.334 at seven, so the slogan comes from a drop below one half at seven. A report of work by the Trefethens says an information-style yardstick would accept five to six; that is a single report, so the page treats it as attributed, not established. The page computes its own numbers and labels them as computed here. 52 factorial is about 8.07e67.

facts.claim: For a 52-card deck under the Gilbert-Shannon-Reeds model, total variation distance from uniform is about 0.924 after five riffles, 0.614 after six and 0.334 after seven.
The distance stays close to 1 through five riffles and falls below one half only at seven riffles, which is where the seven-shuffles slogan comes from.
The number of orderings of a 52-card deck is 52 factorial, about 8.0658e67.

After m riffles of an n-card deck, the probability of an arrangement with r rising sequences is C(2^m + n - r, n) / 2^(mn), so it depends only on r and exact distances can be computed without sampling.

As of 2026-10-10, per Science News, the Trefethens argued that five riffles do a reasonable job and six make mixing practically certain, using an information-style yardstick (single report, unverified).

inspirations: the cutoff phenomenon in Markov chains
magician's faro and riffle control moves

design.coreLoop: The visitor picks an opening deck (new-deck order, suits grouped, lightly pre-shuffled), chooses a cut point by dragging and releases a riffle (or presses auto-riffle), and reads the rising-sequence strands and a meter showing the exact distance from random for that many riffles under the standard model. A yardstick switch (total variation, separation, entropy-style) shows the verdict moving. An audit panel runs seeded Monte Carlo in a worker at 1 to 10 riffles and charts how several simple tests (top card, suit adjacency, a card-guessing duel against the page) betray the opening order, next to the exact curve with a stated sample size and error bar. A seeded daily challenge gives a shareable puzzle: find the smallest riffle count at which a chosen test stops beating chance.
sophisticationHooks: Exact total variation, separation and entropy-style distances for 52 cards by grouping orders by rising-sequence count (Eulerian numbers in BigInt), checked against brute force at n=3 and 4
Yardstick switch so the visitor sees the seven versus five-to-six dispute emerge from the numbers, with every figure labelled computed here
A card-guessing duel: the page guesses each next card by exploiting residual order and its score over chance is charted against riffle count
Hand riffle by pointer drag with keyboard equivalent, and a URL hash carrying seed, opening deck and riffle count
design.scopeForOneDay: Build: seeded GSR sampler, exact distances via Eulerian counts in BigInt, canvas deck renderer with a simple two-pile slide riffle (reduced-motion static fallback), worker Monte Carlo defaulting to about 200k decks with an optional longer run, three simple tests plus the guessing duel, hash state, about panel. Cut: other shuffle types beyond one comparison toggle, sound, a 10-million-shuffle default, per-card art.
risks: The meter describes the riffle process, not the particular deck on screen, and the hand riffle only chooses the cut with interleaving drawn by the model; the page must say so plainly
The seven versus five-to-six dispute rests on one report; the page shows it as 'as of 2026-10-10, per Science News' or omits it, and presents the entropy meter as its own computation
Ten million riffles at ten counts is too heavy for a worker in a visitor's patience; the default is a few hundred thousand decks with a stated error bar
Exact computation for 52 cards needs BigInt or log-space arithmetic; node self-checks against n=3 and 4 brute force
Riffle animation art could eat the morning; keep to a two-pile slide animation

verification.notes: The 0.924/0.614/0.334 figures, the rising-sequence formula and 52 factorial each came back in independent search results; no page could be opened (all fetches failed on DNS). The entropy-yardstick claim rests on one report and is shown only as attributed; scope trimmed (smaller default Monte Carlo, meter wording fixed).
